    【During Test】

historical_reviews.deepseek: YES submits `TEMP_CRPS1~2` as one literal record and cannot prove two PSU readings. It does not bind CRPS1/2 to physical slots, module serials, PMBus pages or temperature fields, define active/standby/absent semantics, or provide complete threshold/UI/freshness evidence.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly calls for vendor PMBus documentation, separate reads and no PSU manipulation. V3.1 further separates CRPS1/2 from the adjacent six-PSU family and requires per-module serial, AC feed, redundancy/load-share state and exact PMBus temperature object so neither generic PSU numbering nor a different temperature channel substitutes.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 892/2291 accepts a literal range query and output presence without two physical CRPS modules, slot/serial/PMBus mapping, redundancy state or complete threshold and UI correlation.
historical_reviews.related_source_cases: Wistron-BMC-00077-V003 separately requests threshold/assert-deassert behavior for `TEMP_CRPS1~TEMP_CRPS2`; its heat-to-threshold language does not authorize thermal stimulus in this passive Sensor Page case. Adjacent `TEMP_PSU1~6` is a different sensor family and cannot fill CRPS coverage.

original_test_intent: Verify `TEMP_CRPS1` and `TEMP_CRPS2` are the two intended common-redundant-power-supply temperature records and are individually readable in Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading with correct physical module, PMBus measurement point, value, units, status and supported thresholds.
original_method: Confirm CRPS terminology and the two-module population, map each index to physical slot, serial, AC feed and PMBus page/object, then compare complete passive raw/UI fields with the applicable inlet, internal or outlet temperature limits under recorded power draw, load sharing and cooling. Preserve PSU, BMC and SEL state.
manual_activity: The power owner defines CRPS1/2 versus PSU1-6, maps both modules to slot, serial, feed and PMBus temperature field, and supplies state-dependent limits. Automation can collect both passive records, PSU inventory and UI rows; a human confirms the physical/redundancy state and owns the verdict. No PSU hot-swap, AC-feed or load change is authorized.
required_inputs: Chassis and power-subsystem PN/revision, BMC/PSU firmware and authoritative CRPS definition
CRPS1/2 bay, AC feed, PN/serial/HW/FW, rated capacity and presence/active/standby/load-share state
Vendor PMBus Application Note or firmware specification with controller/bus/mux/address/page/command and exact temperature-field semantics
Stable SDR and Dashboard/Server Health identities for both modules
Per-field units, scaling, tolerance, thresholds/hysteresis, status, polling and unavailable/stale rules
State-specific acceptance for present, active, standby, absent, degraded redundancy and unequal load sharing
Recorded system input/output power, per-module current/load, fan speeds, ambient and airflow
Validated protected ipmitool/API/browser access and pinned reviewed `sensor.git` revision/checksum or manual method
safety_requirements: Do not clear SEL, kernel, PSU black-box or PMBus evidence; prior power and thermal events are relevant.
Do not issue `sensor get 'TEMP_CRPS1~2'` unless documented as one record. Enumerate and query CRPS1 and CRPS2 separately.
Do not assume CRPS index equals the adjacent PSU1-6 numbering. Bind each reading to bay, serial, AC feed and PMBus page/object.
Treat PMBus/I2C/I3C as BMC/platform-management scope and use only supported read-only access; host-side bus listing does not prove the intended module or field.
Do not hot-remove/reseat a PSU, disconnect AC, change load sharing/redundancy, start power stress, alter fan/threshold policy or write PMBus commands. Record the existing state.

Do not truncate inventory, expose passwords with `-P`, assume cipher 17 or execute the inaccessible Script. Stop without automatic retry on missing/swapped modules, stale data or BMC/UI/PMBus disagreement.
agent_execution_scope: Validate the CRPS population and two-module slot/serial/feed/PMBus map, target, client, vendor specification and Script; build a two-row expectation matrix.
Retrieve CRPS1 and CRPS2 independently with full SDR/PMBus identity, temperature-field meaning, value, units, supported thresholds, status and timestamp; capture both unchanged UI rows.
Correlate each reading with passive inventory, active/standby/load-share state and recorded input/output load, fans, ambient and airflow; do not change these conditions.
Preserve raw/redacted evidence and logs; perform no clear, hot-swap, AC/load/redundancy, fan/threshold/PMBus write, automatic retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve the CRPS definition and two-module bay/serial/feed/PMBus-field map, distinct from PSU1-6.
Provide state- and field-specific limits, tolerance, threshold/status/freshness and absent/degraded rules; approve the read-only tool/Script.
Review both modules independently and issue the formal verdict without substituting one module, a generic PSU sensor or aggregate power health.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Unfit as written because tilde shorthand is not an IPMI wildcard and one response cannot prove two CRPS modules. It omits bay/serial/feed/PMBus-field and redundancy-state mapping, truncates fallback data, exposes credentials and assumes cipher support.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Enumerate both module records, confirm bay/serial/feed and vendor PMBus fields, query each through protected read-only access, and correlate both UI rows with the state-specific specification.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: TEMP_CRPS1~2, Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading, readability/specification Criteria, generic clear text, Script URL, DeepSeek commands and 1/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review expands the range without editing Master or changing the power subsystem.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a two-row matrix keyed by CRPS bay/serial/feed and PMBus page/object, recording active/standby/load-share state and comparing complete raw/API and UI fields with state- and field-specific limits under the unchanged power/cooling condition.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The exact CRPS population and BMC/PMBus/SDR/WebUI build documented by the Project.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record chassis/power-subsystem, BMC, each PSU HW/FW/PMBus revision, WebUI/SDR, management client and Script revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Power-subsystem wiring and bay map, PSU inventory, vendor PMBus Application Note/firmware specification, BMC SDR definition, WebUI schema and Project power recipe.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Resolves the range into two serial- and PMBus-field-bound modules and adds redundancy/load-share context while preserving passive display coverage.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Static temperatures do not validate PSU hot-swap, AC redundancy, load sharing, efficiency, fault ride-through, black-box logging, threshold events or shutdown protection.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Two-module identity/PMBus map, state-specific acceptance, passive sampling timing, protected tool or reviewed Script and evidence contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Firmware may expose multiple temperature channels and remap PMBus pages; standby modules can legitimately report different values or unavailable fields depending on design.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use Redfish/OEM or vendor PMBus tooling as an approved alternative/corroboration only while preserving the original ipmitool method, recording interface/version/page/object and reason, obtaining engineer approval and proving equivalent separate CRPS1/2 identity, field, value, threshold, status and freshness coverage. Generic PSU1-6 telemetry is not automatically equivalent.
expected_evidence: Chassis/power-subsystem PN/revision, BMC and both CRPS bay/feed/PN/serial/HW/FW/capacity/presence/state identities
Vendor PMBus reference plus controller/bus/mux/address/page/command and exact temperature-field map for CRPS1 and CRPS2
Complete separate raw records with stable IDs, values, units, threshold capabilities/values, status and timestamps plus redacted Dashboard/Server Health rows
Recorded input/output power, per-module load-share/active-standby state, fan/ambient/airflow and state-specific tolerance comparison

Explicit absent/degraded/missing/swapped/stale/divergent disposition, pinned Script/tool security evidence, no-clear/no-hot-swap/no-feed-or-load-change/no-retry proof, final PSU/BMC health and engineer-owned two-module verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The literal range and CRPS/PMBus details are underdefined, but Items, UI Procedure and Criteria consistently request passive display/specification validation of two CRPS temperatures. Exact module and field mapping is readiness, not a conflicting purpose.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The two-module passive CRPS temperature purpose is identifiable. Vendor PMBus documentation and Project power mapping can supply the missing execution inputs, so the review is not permanently BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Prevents a failed range query, generic PSU sensor or wrong PMBus temperature channel from being presented as two CRPS modules, and prevents PSU hot-swap, AC-feed or load manipulation from being added to a passive display test.
independent_technical_reasoning: CRPS telemetry is module- and firmware-specific: multiple PMBus temperature objects can represent inlet, internal or outlet locations, while page and slot mappings may change. Two readable numbers are insufficient without serial/feed/field identity and current load-sharing state. Passive UI validation provides no authority for PSU or AC manipulation.
